notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/upihandle.guide.tsx, self-contained) and docs/evidence/upihandle.md at cba512f (“docs: publish the 5 October Coin build's component fixes”, 8 October), the same blobs on main and docs-next. The guide's Sources note was checked on 8 October 2026 on the 5 October build, which the evidence's 636f3f5 check names (mirror v0.1.78-636f3f5, Biscuit's main at 636f3f5), so items citing the note or that check carry 2026-10-08 and 0.1.78-636f3f5 (same package version as installed, so the trace check does not flag them). The evidence's first check (1 October, 0.1.77) is out of date where its 636f3f5 section says #182 is fixed: the pressable UPI Handle now has role button and a name, accessibilityLabel is no longer ignored, disabled is dimmed, a click adds no border or layout shift, the UPI Handle shrinks, and there is a style prop; the Storybook MDX line that accessibilityLabel is forced to undefined is out of date too. None of those sentences is used, and no 0.1.77 line is quoted (its still-true lines, source forcing UPI Handle Image, untinted avatars and the 0.98 press scale, are package facts here). Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Builds compared through gh api: UpiHandle.tsx is the same blob (0deb977) at v0.1.78-636f3f5, v0.1.78-dbe0e02 and in node_modules (its last change is 636f3f5; v0.1.78 at 5b6894b had a2cb173); the design-tokens JSON (4545aec), resolver (d03e77c), JFSThemeProvider and figma-modes are identical at both tags; react-utils, typography and MediaSource are unchanged since 0.1.77; web-platform-utils.ts changed at c1fa197 only in useKeyboardActivation, which UpiHandle doesn't use (isKeyboardInputModality and keyboardFocusRingStyle, lines 241–281, are unchanged); Icon.tsx changed at a116616 only in its loading Skeleton, and UpiHandle passes no loading. So nothing the 8 October check read has changed. Every guide sentence quoted here was read against the installed UpiHandle.tsx (read, not rendered; token values through the package's own getVariableByName in lib/commonjs): the UPI Handle is a centred row on upiHandle/background rgb(245, 245, 245) with radius 99999 (fully rounded), 14 px padding at each end, 4 px on the left when UPI Handle Image is True, 3 px vertical, a 6 px gap, maxWidth 100%, flexShrink 1 and alignSelf flex-start, so it hugs its content and can shrink (lines 100–113); the label is 12 px on a 23 px line, so the UPI Handle is 29 px tall, and it is one line ending in an ellipsis unless disableTruncation is set (120–128, 272–279; react-utils.ts 171–180); the avatar is 23 px and the icon 12 px (85–86, 97, 131–134); label defaults to “Label”, showIcon to true and iconName to ic_scan_qr_code (162–165), and ic_copy and ic_scan_qr_code are both in the icon registry (registry.ts 1253, 4016); a source (or avatarSource) forces UPI Handle Image True and no source forces False, over any value in modes (184–191), the avatar renders only then (193, 261–271), and MediaSource gets no tint (263–269); with onPress or onClick (227–228) the UPI Handle is a Pressable with role button, named by accessibilityLabel or else the label (293, 300–301, 306 on the web), scaled to 0.98 while pressed unless disabled (27, 240); disabled sets opacity 0.5 (233), Pressable disabled, aria-disabled and tabIndex -1 on the web (302–312); keyboard focus on the web draws a 1 px outline 2 px out in mode/Grey/200 (218–221, 230–232; web-platform-utils.ts 274–281), which takes no layout room, and a pointer or mouse down clears keyboard modality, so a click leaves no ring (web-platform-utils.ts 241–266); without onPress the UPI Handle is a View with role text (324–334); the component never copies or opens anything itself, it only calls onPress (311). The guide's Sizing example's style={{ maxWidth: 140 }} is how the 636f3f5 check saw truncation in the browser; the maxWidth 100% case is read from source, as the evidence says. No guide sentence is contradicted, so there is no guide fix and no reviews file. Out of date and not used: the Sources note's “Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (5 October build)” (the installed build is now 27 October, with UpiHandle unchanged). Not recorded: disableTruncation, avatarSource (deprecated), accessibilityHint, testID and the inherited View props (no guide sentence); the Figma size (144 × 29) and the measure labels (130.5 × 29, Shown at 2×); the Storybook story list; context 10 and Profile Card Appearance (no guide sentence: context 10 jioPlus turns the UPI Handle navy, rgb(2, 24, 145), with a white label, which ProfileCard sets on its handles; Premium alone changes no upiHandle token) and Color Mode (building rules); the playground and its readout. Anatomy: Handle and Background are always present; Avatar appears only with a source; Action icon is optional (showIcon), though by default a scan icon shows. avoidWhen keeps the guide's Combine handles Don't, without useInstead (the answer is one UPI Handle per ID). The style rule rests on the package's style fact, not on the 140 px example alone. The gap is the evidence's still-open Figma difference (Figma's copy icon, the package's scan default), which still holds on dbe0e02 (line 165); the 636f3f5 check says it was not in #182's Expected, so the gap names no ticket. Strength: three quotes hold “only”: the In context sentence (everywhere: the component only reports the press), the icon sentence and “Display only” (contextual: both name the display-only case). Nothing is required. content.good is the guide's Content handles; bad is its placeholder and combined-handles Don'ts. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every UpiHandle, Card, VStack, Text and Button) and no other modes. Confirm the payee is the guide's In context composition (a Card holding a VStack with a Text, the UPI Handle and the Pay Button, lines 90–94), with the guide's inline SVG sample avatar (sample content, as the evidence says) replaced by a URI for the payee's photo, and its status readout left out; Without avatar is the guide's Copy helper (lines 17–19: iconName ic_copy, accessibilityLabel “Copy ” + label, onPress) on shrutirai-1@jio (line 50); Display only is its No icon card (line 52). Card, VStack and Button have guide entries; Text has an undocumented entry. Left out of examples (three at most): the anatomy specimen, the With avatar and Scan icon cards, the States cards, the Sizing measure and its Long handles truncate example, the Content handles, the Do & Don'ts and the playground. Consistency: profilecard.json is the only other entry that mentions UPI Handle. It agrees: its handles use ic_copy with onPress for a handle people copy, a pressable UPI Handle scales to 0.98, and the screen does the copying through onPress. Its gap “A long UPI handle never ends in …” (checked on c7d3348) concerns ProfileCard's wrapper; its own notes say the installed source now lets the handle end in … inside the card, which matches this entry's sizing rule. Two differences, reported for the coordinator, not edited: ProfileCard's guide puts ic_confirm on a verified number with no onPress (a static UPI Handle with an icon, profilecard /content/rules/6 and examples 0–1), while this guide says to choose the icon for the UPI Handle's action or none, and calls the icon a cue for what pressing does (the 1 October evidence says Storybook's docs name ic_confirm for a verified handle); and ProfileCard's handle type has no accessibilityLabel (ProfileCard.tsx 27–36, 347–354), so a copy UPI Handle inside a ProfileCard is named by its handle only. Sorting (batch 14, two cross-check runs). Round 1 flagged /facts/gaps/0: the gap added the guide's advice to set ic_copy, which the evidence line doesn't say; our misreading, so the gap now keeps to the evidence and the advice stays in /configuration/5 (Sources). Round 2 raised no flags. Its notes, not flags: /useWhen/1 reads the In context heading as a use (a reading of the title, kept as recommended); /examples/0's Card holding a VStack is the guide's own code (upihandle.guide.tsx lines 90–94), which the rendered copy can't show; /accessibility/1's fallback to the handle is stated by the guide's Sources note, and the installed source bears it out (UpiHandle.tsx 293, 301 and 306: accessibilityLabel || label), though the evidence says it was read from source, not browser-checked. No dismissals, no guide fix, no Component Bug. Left: none from the checks; the entry is documented once this cross-check stands. Refreshed 29 October 2026 for guide fix #543 (3f56271): the guide and evidence now say UPI Handle, or a grey rounded background for the surface (Anatomy part “Background”), and the second Do is “One ID per UPI Handle”; every item that quoted the old wording quotes the new sentence, and /avoidWhen/0, /configuration/8, /states/2 and the disabled fact say UPI Handle in their own words. No flag, dismissal or gap changed.

placementAdvice.text: Let the screen do the work: it copies the handle or opens the payment when the UPI Handle is pressed; the UPI Handle only reports the press, through onPress.

absolute.reason: it describes every UPI Handle: the installed component has no copy or payment logic of its own and only calls onPress (or its alias onClick) when pressed (UpiHandle.tsx lines 227 and 311, 0.1.78-dbe0e02).

examples.purpose: Confirm the payee, the guide's In context: a Card with the payee's name in a Text, the payee's UPI Handle with an avatar and the copy icon, and the Pay Button, stacked in a VStack as the guide's code stacks them. The UPI Handle's onPress stands for the screen copying the handle, and the Button's for the screen starting the payment. The URI stands for the payee's own photo.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <Text>Paying Priya Sharma</Text>
    <UpiHandle
      label="priya@jio"
      source={{ uri: 'https://example.com/photos/priya-sharma.jpg' }}
      iconName="ic_copy"
      accessibilityLabel="Copy priya@jio"
      onPress={() => {}}
    />
    <Button label="Pay ₹500" onPress={() => {}} />
  </VStack>
</Card>
